subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In a graph of photosynthesis rate against light intensity, what does a plateau region indicate?
options: A factor other than light, such as CO2 or temperature, is now limiting
Light is the limiting factor
Photosynthesis has stopped completely
Respiration exceeds photosynthesis
questions.explain: Once the curve plateaus, increasing light has no effect, so another factor limits the rate.

questions.q: At high substrate concentration with fixed enzyme concentration, the rate of reaction plateaus because:
options: the enzyme has denatured
the substrate is used up
all active sites are occupied so enzyme concentration becomes the limiting factor
the pH has changed
questions.explain: When substrate is in excess, every active site is continually occupied, so the number of enzyme molecules limits the rate.

questions.q: What is the approximate respiratory quotient (RQ) for the complete aerobic respiration of a carbohydrate such as glucose?
questions.explain: For glucose the volumes of CO2 produced and O2 consumed are equal, giving an RQ of 1.0.

questions.q: Which feature of the chloroplast increases the surface area available for the light-dependent reactions?
options: The stacked thylakoid membranes forming grana
The double outer envelope
The fluid-filled stroma
The presence of starch grains
questions.explain: Thylakoids stacked into grana give a large membrane surface area for photosystems and electron carriers.

questions.q: A competitive inhibitor reduces the rate of an enzyme-catalysed reaction by:
options: permanently denaturing the enzyme
binding to the active site, having a similar shape to the substrate
binding away from the active site and changing the active site shape
increasing the Vmax of the reaction
questions.explain: A competitive inhibitor has a complementary shape to the active site and competes with substrate for it; its effect is overcome by raising substrate concentration.

questions.q: In the Calvin cycle, what is the role of ATP and reduced NADP in converting GP to triose phosphate (TP)?
options: They catalyse photolysis of water
ATP oxidises GP while NADP fixes carbon
They regenerate RuBP directly from CO2
ATP provides energy and reduced NADP provides hydrogen to reduce GP to TP
questions.explain: GP is reduced to triose phosphate using energy from ATP and hydrogen from reduced NADP.

questions.q: When CO2 is fixed onto the 5-carbon RuBP, what is the immediate product?
options: One molecule of glucose
One molecule of reduced NADP
Two molecules of glycerate-3-phosphate (GP)
One molecule of triose phosphate
questions.explain: The unstable 6-carbon intermediate splits at once into two 3-carbon molecules of GP.

questions.q: Which is the correct order of stages in aerobic respiration?
options: Link reaction then glycolysis then Krebs cycle then oxidative phosphorylation
Glycolysis then link reaction then Krebs cycle then oxidative phosphorylation
Krebs cycle then glycolysis then oxidative phosphorylation then link reaction
Glycolysis then Krebs cycle then link reaction then oxidative phosphorylation
questions.explain: Glucose is split in glycolysis, pyruvate enters the link reaction, then the Krebs cycle, then oxidative phosphorylation.

questions.q: A coenzyme differs from a prosthetic group in that a coenzyme:
options: is a small organic molecule that binds temporarily and is often derived from vitamins
is part of the protein's primary structure
is a permanently bound metal ion
is an inorganic cofactor
questions.explain: Coenzymes are loosely bound organic molecules, frequently vitamin-derived, that participate transiently, unlike permanently bound prosthetic groups.

questions.q: Why does a very high temperature reduce the rate of the light-independent reactions?
options: It speeds photolysis excessively
It increases CO2 solubility too much
It stops light absorption by chlorophyll
It denatures enzymes such as RuBisCO
questions.explain: Excessive heat denatures the enzymes of the Calvin cycle, including RuBisCO, slowing the reactions.

questions.q: Which statement about the role of reduced NAD and reduced FAD in respiration is correct?
options: They are the final electron acceptors of the chain
They are produced only during oxidative phosphorylation
They directly phosphorylate ADP to ATP
They deliver electrons and protons to the electron transport chain
questions.explain: Reduced coenzymes carry electrons and protons to the carriers on the inner membrane, feeding the chain.

the rate of reaction at zero substrate
the optimum temperature for the enzyme
the substrate concentration at which the enzyme denatures
questions.explain: Vmax is the theoretical maximum rate achieved when enzyme active sites are fully saturated and working at capacity.
